page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c1.small is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs and 8.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a resource density of 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage, requiring external block storage volumes for persistent data. Additionally, it does not feature any GPU hardware accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

A key technical characteristic of the ecs.c1.small instance is the absence of advanced CPU instruction sets. The processor configuration lacks support for Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX, AVX512), Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), and hardware-accelerated cryptography standards such as AES or SHA-NI. It also lacks virtualization extensions (VMX, SVM) and common bit manipulation instructions (BMI2, FMA). These omissions represent a significant performance tradeoff for workloads relying on vectorization, encryption, or nested virtualization.

Given the low memory-to-CPU ratio and the lack of modern instruction sets, this instance represents a legacy or highly specialized hardware profile. It offers a high density of dedicated vCPUs relative to memory, which can be qualitatively cost-efficient for basic parallel processing tasks that are not memory-intensive. Appropriate workloads include legacy multi-threaded applications, basic web serving, lightweight batch processing, and CPU-bound tasks that do not require modern vector or matrix acceleration.
